executive_summary: NZD/USD closed the gated weekday store at 0.5642 on 2026-09-29 and traded 0.5622 on the valuation date, its lowest since November 2025, after falling 4.64% in one month, 1.00% over three, 0.92% over six and 1.79% over twelve; the BIS real effective exchange rate is 102.84 for August 2026, at the 44th percentile of its January-2024-onward cached history and flat on the year (-0.17 points). The dominant narrative is a currency caught between a central bank that is tightening into an imported-fuel inflation shock and a dollar that is rising faster: the RBNZ under Governor Anna Breman raised the OCR 25bp to 2.75% on 2026-09-02, the second hike since July, and markets now price about a 75% chance of a third move to 3.00% on 2026-10-28, yet the Fed's hike to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and a 51bp jump in the US 10-year to 5.24% left the OCR 125bp below the Fed's upper bound and 185bp below the RBA's 4.60%. Headline CPI is 4.1% but the RBNZ's sectoral factor core is 2.7% and unemployment is 5.6%, the highest since 2015, so the hikes are defensive rather than a sign of a hot economy; Brent at $100.56 drove a 9.0% fall in the terms of trade in Q2 even as dairy held up and Fonterra raised its 2026/27 milk price midpoint to $9.50/kgMS. On PPP the kiwi is 16.9% cheap against the US dollar and 15.0% cheap against the Australian dollar, and AUD/NZD sits at 1.2384, the 94th percentile of its 52-week closing range. The central tension is that domestic rate momentum is now NZD-positive while every fast-moving global input - the dollar, US yields, oil and risk appetite - is NZD-negative. We are Bearish tactically (conviction 2, net score -0.159) and Neutral strategically (conviction 2, net score -0.066): over four weeks the dollar and the technical break below all three daily moving averages dominate, while over six months a narrowing policy gap to the Fed and the RBA offsets the oil-driven terms-of-trade drag. Our six-month NZD/USD base case is 0.5660, below the Trading Economics path of 0.57 at end-Q4 and 0.58 at twelve months.

tactical.analysis: The RBNZ raised the Official Cash Rate 25bp to 2.75% on 2026-09-02, unanimously and by consensus, its second hike since the 8 July move to 2.50%, which places New Zealand fifth of ten rate-setters in G10+SGD: below the RBA (4.60%, +185bp over NZD), Norges Bank (4.50%, +175bp), the Fed (4.00% upper bound, +125bp) and the BoE (3.75%, +100bp), and above the ECB deposit rate (2.50%, -25bp), the BoC (2.25%, -50bp), the Riksbank (1.75%, -100bp), the BoJ (1.25%, -150bp) and the SNB (0.00%, -275bp). The 2-year NZGB yield is 3.92% and the 10-year 5.12%, the latter up 33bp in a month and the highest since November 2023, which gives a steep 2s10s of +120bp against +32bp in the US and +40bp in Australia. The 2-year sits 117bp above the OCR, consistent with roughly 100bp of hikes priced over two years against an RBNZ track that peaks at 3.28%, so the market is about 50bp more hawkish than the central bank's own published path. For the next meeting on 2026-10-28 the market prices about a 75% chance of a 25bp hike to 3.00%, up from 30% straight after the September statement, because Governor Breman said persistent oil prices would push near-term inflation above the September assumptions. We put the October hike at 70%, essentially in line, so the tactical edge on the RBNZ itself is small. The bilateral picture is the problem: the NZ-US 2-year spread is -100bp (3.92% vs 4.92%) and the NZ-AU 2-year spread -108bp (3.92% vs 5.00%), and both the Fed and the RBA hiked 25bp in September, so the kiwi's relative rate position did not improve despite its own hike. Carry pays the short side against the dollar and the Australian dollar and the long side only against the low-yielders, which is why the factor is Neutral over four weeks.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the relative-rate trajectory turns in the kiwi's favour, which is the strongest NZD-positive force in this dossier. The RBNZ is early in a hiking cycle that began in July from 2.25%: we expect 3.00% in October and 3.25% by the 2027-03-17 Monetary Policy Statement, with the December statement lifting the published track from a 3.28% peak toward 3.50%. ANZ is more aggressive at 3.50% by March 2027 and Westpac, as republished by ActionForex (best available, flagged), sees 3.00% by December and 4.00% by September 2027, so the bank range is 3.25-3.50% at the end of our window. Against that, the Fed's median dot of 4.1% for both end-2026 and end-2027 implies at most one more hike, the RBA at 4.60% is at or near its peak after three 2026 hikes, Norges Bank signals a plateau at 4.50%, and the BoC and Riksbank are on hold-to-ease paths. On our path the NZ-US policy gap narrows from -125bp to -100bp or -75bp and the NZ-AU gap from -185bp to -135bp, and the gap to the euro widens from +25bp to +75bp. That is the mechanism that historically pulls AUD/NZD down from extremes: the cross is at the 94th percentile of its 52-week range while the front-end differential is set to compress. The risk to the view is that the market's 2-year at 3.92% already prices more than our path, so the narrowing is partly in the price; the narrowing is in the policy rate, not in the 2-year, and spot follows the former when realised. We are Bullish strategically at 56 (lowered from 58 at the verification gate because the Westpac path figures come from a secondary republication), limited by the fact that the RBNZ is hiking against weak activity rather than strong demand, which caps the number of hikes the economy can absorb.

tactical.analysis: Headline CPI rose 1.5% q/q and 4.1% y/y in the June 2026 quarter, the highest in two years and above the RBNZ's July assumption of 3.9%, but the overshoot is imported: tradables inflation is 4.9% y/y on petrol up 20.1% q/q and diesel up 47.7%, while non-tradables eased to 3.4% from 3.5%. The RBNZ's preferred sectoral factor model core is 2.7%, unchanged for a second quarter and inside the 1-3% band, the 30% trimmed mean is 2.6% and the weighted median 2.7%, so underlying inflation is near the top of the band rather than above it. The next print, the September-quarter CPI on 2026-10-21, is the swing event of the tactical window: consensus is 3.9% y/y and the RBNZ's own September assumption is 0.8% q/q, and with Brent up 5.15% in September we see risk of 4.0% or higher, which would validate the 75% October hike pricing. Growth is soft but not collapsing: GDP rose 0.2% q/q in Q2 against a 0.1% consensus and a flat RBNZ forecast, with 2.6% y/y, but real gross national disposable income fell 0.4% because of the terms-of-trade loss. Unemployment rose to 5.6%, the highest since September 2015, even as employment grew 0.5% q/q, and private-sector LCI wage growth is only 2.0% y/y. Leading indicators are mixed and fading: ANZ business confidence 51.9 (from 53.7), expected own activity 47.9 with late-month responses at 36, BusinessNZ PMI 53.1, PSI 51.2 and Westpac consumer sentiment 89.5. Hot imported inflation and soft domestic growth offset each other for the currency over four weeks, so the stance is Neutral. The June-quarter CPI was published on 2026-07-21, older than the 30-day tactical window; it is the latest print and is flagged as best available until 2026-10-21, which is why confidence is 51.

strategic.analysis: Over six months the inflation-growth mix turns against the kiwi because the inflation is transitory and the growth weakness is not. The RBNZ itself expects inflation to return to the 1-3% band by mid-2027 as fuel effects drop out of the annual calculation, and with core at 2.7% and one-year business inflation expectations at 3.25% that projection is credible, which limits how far the hiking cycle can run. Meanwhile the real economy is absorbing a 9.0% terms-of-trade loss in a single quarter: real national disposable income fell 0.4% in Q2, per-capita GDP rose only 0.1%, unemployment is at a nine-year high of 5.6% and the RBNZ expects only a 0.1pp dip to 5.5% in Q3. Housing, the dominant wealth channel in New Zealand, is flat to falling: the REINZ house price index was unchanged in July and down 0.4% y/y, sales were down 10% y/y and days to sell 46.9, with Auckland down 1.7% and Wellington down 4.4%, and higher mortgage rates after the 10-year's 91bp rise in a year will lean on it further. The ANZ survey shows activity expectations deteriorating within September (52 early, 36 late) and employment intentions easing to 17.9. The bull case - construction up 2.7% in Q2, residential construction intentions jumping to 22.2 and exports to China up 15.8% - is real but narrow. A central bank hiking into stagnant real incomes is not a durable source of currency strength, so the factor is Bearish strategically at 53, trimmed at the verification gate because the CPI print (2026-07-21) and the July REINZ data are older than the freshness windows (best available, flagged).

tactical.analysis: Global risk appetite is not broken but it is deteriorating at the margin, and the kiwi is the G10 currency most exposed to that margin. VIX closed at 16.07 on 2026-09-28, up 1.64 points in a month but below the 20 level usually associated with stress, so equity volatility is not signalling stress. Credit is more informative: the US high-yield option-adjusted spread widened 42bp in a month to 302bp and the investment-grade spread is 83bp, so credit is cheapening from tight levels as energy-driven inflation pushes Treasury yields up. The S&P 500 is 7,681.58, up 14.39% over a year but only 0.20% over the past month, with the latest session led lower by financials and industrials on rising yields and stalled US-Iran talks. The regime is a transition from risk-on to a rates-driven risk-off, in which high-beta, low-liquidity currencies underperform even without an equity drawdown. The kiwi's beta is visible in the crosses: NZD/JPY, the purest G10 risk barometer, fell 6.11% in a month against a 2.51% fall in AUD/USD and a 4.64% fall in NZD/USD, so the kiwi moved roughly 1.8 times the Australian dollar against the US dollar. The correlation structure is intact - kiwi down with credit spreads wider and yields higher - which means there is no idiosyncratic support to lean on. The two tail scenarios that would shift the regime are a US-Iran settlement that takes Brent below $85 (risk-on, kiwi-positive) and a credit event that takes high-yield spreads above 400bp (risk-off, kiwi-negative); we see the second as somewhat more likely inside four weeks because the US 10-year is at 5.24%.

The bear case is a rates-led tightening of financial conditions: a US 10-year above 5% with core inflation still above target, credit spreads that have already widened 42bp in a month and an oil shock that keeps the Fed hawkish, all of which hurt a high-beta currency that has no Fed swap line and thin liquidity outside Asia-Pacific hours. tactical.analysis: The RBNZ's communication has turned decisively hawkish over the past four months, and that shift is the kiwi's main domestic support. In May the Committee held at 2.25% on the Governor's casting vote after a 3-3 split; by July it hiked to 2.50% and on 2026-09-02 it hiked again to 2.75% by unanimous consensus, stating that 'gradually removing monetary stimulus is consistent with achieving the medium-term inflation target' and that the future path is 'not pre-determined'. The published OCR track was left with a 3.28% peak and a Q4-2026 average of 2.81%, which mechanically implied only about 20% odds of an October hike, and the 2-year swap fell 7-8bp on the day. Since then Governor Anna Breman has said that 'if higher oil prices persist, they are expected to result in somewhat higher near-term inflation than we assumed in the September Statement', and October hike pricing jumped from about 57% to 75%: the market now runs ahead of the track because the Governor invited it to. The next communication is the 2026-10-28 Monetary Policy Review, which is a decision without a new track; the RBNZ typically does not lean against pricing it has itself validated. Credibility on inflation is intact: longer-term inflation expectations are near 2% and business expectations are 3.25%. The stance is Bullish at 55 because the gap between the 3.28% track and market pricing is more likely to close by the RBNZ moving up in December than by the market moving down.

The December MPS on 2026-12-09 will almost certainly raise the track from a 3.28% peak, and Westpac's view of 4.00% by September 2027 shows how far a hawkish reading could go. The November 7 election adds a fiscal variable to the RBNZ's reaction function. tactical.analysis: The tactical window holds an unusually dense cluster of binary New Zealand events. The September-quarter CPI on 2026-10-21 decides whether the 75% October hike pricing holds; the RBNZ decision on 2026-10-28 lands on the same day as the FOMC and the Bank of Canada, so the kiwi's reaction will be filtered through the dollar within hours; and two GDT auctions, on 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-20, can each move NZD/USD 30-50 pips on a 3-5% index move. The geopolitical overlay is the US-Iran conflict around the Strait of Hormuz: Brent at $100.56 carries a war premium, PetroChina has withdrawn fuel cargoes and negotiations have made little progress, so a settlement or an escalation are both live. Our tail estimates for moves above 2% in NZD/USD within four weeks are a Hormuz settlement that takes Brent below $85 (15%, kiwi up 2-3%), a credit-led risk-off with high-yield spreads above 400bp (10%, kiwi down 3-4%) and an RBNZ hold on 2026-10-28 against 75% pricing (25%, kiwi down 1-1.5%). Over four weeks the only fiscal catalyst is campaign promises ahead of the 2026-11-07 election, which have not moved the bond market. The stance is Neutral at 58.

assumptions: Policy rates are taken from Data-Cache/calendar/events actuals for the most recent decision, not from the CBPOL_ series, per the cycle correction. NZD is 2.75% (event store, RBNZ Interest Rate Decision 2026-09-02, actual 2.75, previous 2.5; CBPOL_NZ agrees at 2.75 as of 2026-09-18) and is confirmed by the RBNZ release [1]. Peers: AUD 4.60 (2026-09-29), CAD 2.25, CHF 0.00, EUR 2.50 deposit / 2.65 MRO, GBP 3.75, JPY 1.25 (2026-09-18), NOK 4.50 (2026-09-24), SEK 1.75, USD 4.00 upper / 3.875 effective. The derived/*.json rates blocks carry stale AUD 4.35, NOK 4.25 and JPY 1.00 legs (cycle Defect 1b), so no differential was taken from them; all spreads and carry were recomputed.

Rate conventions: EUR is the ECB deposit facility rate of 2.50% (MRO 2.65%, spread to NZD -10bp); USD is the federal funds target upper bound of 4.00% (3.875% effective, spread +112.5bp, used for the funding-basis residual); SGD has no policy rate.

The cached Brent series (DCOILBRENTEU, 114.89 on 2026-09-22) is treated as corrupt (cycle Defect 3: $18.48 above cached WTI of 96.41 on the same day) and is not quoted. The live Brent print used is $100.56 on 2026-10-01 from Trading Economics [21].

CPI in the macro comparison table is the most recent PUBLISHED print per country with the period labelled. NZ uses the Stats NZ June-quarter print (4.1%) and the RBNZ sectoral factor model (2.7%) [7][8]; US uses the August CPI (3.4%) rather than the 2026-Q2 OECD vintage; SEK core is CPIF ex energy 0.5% for August, verified against Trading Economics [40] (the 1.60 in the JPY dossier is wrong). Peer CPI and core figures are cross-checked against the Trading Economics country lists [38][39]; GDP, unemployment and current account are OECD/Eurostat point-in-time vintages as of 2026-10-01.

Sovereign yields: NZ 2-year 3.92% and 10-year 5.12% (2026-10-01) [6] and Australia 2-year 5.00% and 10-year 5.40% (2026-10-01) [35] are live web prints; the US 2-year (4.92%) and 10-year (5.24%) are cached daily DGS2/DGS10 for 2026-09-28. UK, Japan, Switzerland and Canada 10-year yields are monthly IRLTLT01 vintages (2026-08-01, Canada 2026-06-01) and are labelled stale; the cached NZ 10-year (4.71%, monthly 2026-08-01) is superseded by the live print.

Realised volatility is read from realisedVol in Data-Cache/derived/{PAIR}.json (60-day for carry-to-vol), never estimated or built from two USD legs. NZD/SEK has no price file, so its carry-to-vol is a documented gap; its PPP spot is the product of the NZD/USD and USD/SEK closes (closes multiply; highs, lows and vol do not).

Implied vol and risk reversals are the CME-derived values in Data-Cache/derived/NZDUSD.json (cme_atm, observed 2026-09-25) at 41.7, 104.7 and 160.7 days; iv_1m carries the 41.7-day tenor and iv_3m the 104.7-day tenor. The 1Y IV percentile is unavailable: the cached CME history begins 2026-08-21, so the 70 reported is the 3-month ATM's position within 26 observations (best available, flagged). The cross vols for AUD/NZD, EUR/NZD etc. in the cache are triangulated estimates, not quotes.

CFTC positioning is taken from the CFTC Traders in Financial Futures report for 2026-09-22 [24] because the cached COT.csv carries no New Zealand dollar rows (documented); the all-spec net history is the pipeline event store's 'CFTC NZD speculative net positions' series (Aug-Sep 2026), so the reported 56 is a short-window range position, not a multi-year percentile.

Forward points are derived from the cached NZD/USD futures-implied roll premium (+109.5bp annualised, CME calendar spread, observed 2026-09-25) on an actual/365 basis, not quoted. The NZD/USD cross-currency basis is likewise derived as the residual between that premium and the 112.5bp effective policy gap (about -3bp); quoted 3M EUR/USD and JPY/USD basis are unavailable from free sources.

Market-implied RBNZ pricing is taken from cited reports (about 75% for an October hike) and inferred from the 2-year NZGB yield; no free NZ OIS curve was available. The RBNZ's September OCR track figures (3.28% peak, 2.81% Q4 average) come from ANZ's MPS review [2] because the MPS track is published as a chart.

PPP deviations use World Bank PPP conversion factors for 2025 [37] (LCU per international dollar), with Germany as the euro-area proxy; fair value NZD/XXX = PPP(XXX)/PPP(NZD) compared with the 2026-09-29 close. The JPY (+34.6%) and SGD (+34.3%) deviations are dominated by price-level (Balassa-Samuelson) effects and are reported for completeness, not as signals.

The BIS REER percentile (44th) is measured within the 32 monthly observations cached since January 2024, not a long-run history. The RBNZ TWI level, the August REINZ release, the PREFU figures, whole milk powder prices at Event 412, sovereign CDS and the exact Stats NZ release dates for the September-quarter labour market and GDP are documented gaps; those two releases use the YYYY-MM-WN format.

Scheduled central-bank dates come exclusively from Data-Cache/calendar/central-bank-meetings.json (RBNZ 2026-10-28, 2026-12-09, 2027-02-10, 2027-03-17). GDT dates come from the GDT calendar [14] and the Q3 CPI date (2026-10-21) from [5].

Weighted scores are computed in the generator from the factor stances and confidences (Bullish +1, Neutral 0, Bearish -1, times confidence/100, times horizon weight); markdown and JSON are emitted from one data structure. Conviction mapping: |net| < 0.10 Neutral (conviction 1-2); 0.10-0.20 conviction 2; 0.20-0.35 conviction 3; above 0.35 conviction 4-5.

G10+SGD rankings use the net scores of the seven dossiers already published this cycle (AUD, CAD, CHF, EUR, GBP, JPY, NOK) and a qualitative placement of USD, SGD and SEK, whose dossiers are not yet built.

Verification outcome (self-run adversarial gate; no Task tool was available). 102 gated-store values were re-derived directly from Data-Cache rather than from the cache extract - NZD/USD spot, SMA50/100/200 (recomputed from the daily bars), 20d and 60d realised vol (recomputed), performance, 52-week range, ATR, CME implied vols and risk reversals, roll premium, eight crosses (close, 60d vol, 1M/1Y performance, close percentile), AUD/USD 1M, DGS2, DGS10, T10Y2Y, VIX, HY and IG spreads, broad dollar, WTI, the corrupt cached Brent, CBPOL_NZ, five OECD NZL vintages, BIS REER and its 1-year change, thirteen NZD event-store actuals, seven peer rate decisions and the RBNZ, Fed, RBA, Norges Bank, BoE, Riksbank, ECB, BoJ, BoC and SNB meeting dates - and all matched. All 40 citation URLs were fetched in this run and resolved.
